script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. Tuesday — here is your QQQ recap. The portfolio closed down one point six eight percent on the session. A brutal day for semiconductor names drove the damage, and the numbers demand attention.

The chip sell-off that defined Tuesday's session was not surgical — it was broad, deep, and accelerating. Micron fell nearly nine percent. Advanced Micro Devices lost more than eight. Intel dropped close to six. Analysts are calling it indiscriminate panic.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average managed gains on the back of strong earnings from non-technology names, rising roughly five hundred points on the session. The Nasdaq, however, faced significant headwinds as chipmakers broadly sold off ahead of a critical week of Magnificent Seven earnings reports and a Federal Reserve policy meeting. Markets are actively pricing in potential rate movement before year end, though some strategists warn that hiking now would be perilous given current conditions.

The dominant story of Tuesday's session was the semiconductor sector rout, and Micron Technology was at the center of it. Micron closed down eight point eight five percent, landing among the worst performers on the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. This was not an isolated event — the sell-off swept across the entire chip complex, with analysts describing the move as a panic that appears to be indiscriminate rather than driven by company-specific fundamentals. The backdrop is a growing investor debate over whether artificial intelligence infrastructure spending has outpaced near-term revenue realization. Steve Eisman, the investor widely known from the big short trade, publicly warned that crowded artificial intelligence exposure could magnify a correction. Micron represents five point seven five percent of this portfolio, making Tuesday's move one of the single largest individual contributors to the session's decline.

Now the full holdings rundown, largest position first.

Nvidia was up zero point two five percent on the session — a remarkably narrow gain given the carnage elsewhere in semiconductors. Fortune reported analysts describing the chip slump as indiscriminate panic, yet Nvidia held its ground. Watch how it behaves into earnings season as the narrative around artificial intelligence spending intensity continues to develop.

Apple was up zero point nine four percent on the session. The stock approaches Thursday's third quarter earnings call — the final one under chief executive Tim Cook — with investors focused on whether results can sustain Apple's position among the world's most valuable companies. That report is the clearest near-term catalyst for this position.

Alphabet was up two point one nine percent on the session, outperforming the broader technology group meaningfully. Analyst commentary flagged that investors have been pressuring Alphabet and its peers to reduce artificial intelligence data center spending, though voices like Nancy Tengler of Laffer Tengler Investments pushed back, calling this an artificial intelligence arms race that demands continued investment. One note of caution: a separate analysis flagged that Alphabet's profit margin sits at multi-year highs, with gains that may not repeat. Watch the earnings report closely.

Micron Technology was down eight point eight five percent on the session — covered in full in the top story. The position size makes this the most impactful single-name drag on Tuesday's portfolio result.

Microsoft was up one point zero nine percent on the session. Investor debate around big technology artificial intelligence spending is directly relevant here, with Microsoft among the names cited for heavy data center investment. Earnings results are due this week and will be closely watched.

Amazon was down zero point two three percent on the session — essentially flat amid the broader volatility. As with Microsoft, Amazon was named in commentary around investor pressure on artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Earnings are the near-term focus.

Advanced Micro Devices was down eight point one five percent on the session, suffering one of the steeper single-day losses in this portfolio. The move tracked the broader semiconductor sell-off and occurred without company-specific news driving it — reinforcing the indiscriminate nature analysts described. The stock's next significant catalyst will be its own earnings report.

Tesla was down zero point five eight percent on the session. The move was comparatively contained relative to the technology names around it. Consumer discretionary sentiment and broader risk appetite will remain the key variables to monitor here.

Intel was down five point eight six percent on the session. A separate analysis noted Intel has now declined approximately thirty-nine percent since June, raising questions about when the selling exhausts itself. The stock remains a significant drag within this portfolio's technology exposure.

Turning to a substitute for context — Applied Materials fell seven point eight two percent on the session, underscoring that the semiconductor equipment space was hit as hard as chipmakers themselves. Lam Research dropped seven point five four percent, and KLA Corporation declined six point one eight percent. The equipment names confirmed the sell-off was structural across the semiconductor supply chain, not isolated to individual companies.

Three data points to watch over the next forty-eight hours. First, Apple's third quarter earnings report on Thursday, July thirtieth — Tim Cook's final earnings call as chief executive, with margin and services revenue the key metrics. Second, the Federal Reserve policy decision this week under Chair Kevin Warsh, where markets will scrutinize any signal on rate direction. Third, Alphabet's and Microsoft's earnings results, both due this week, which will set the tone for the artificial intelligence spending debate that defined Tuesday's session.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for QQQ. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch the earnings reports from Alphabet and Microsoft closely — how management addresses the artificial intelligence spending debate will likely set the direction for the entire technology complex into the back half of the week.
